methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed preclinical study using multiple liver cancer cell lines (HepG2, Hep3B, SK-HEP-1, THLE-2 normal control). Exosome isolation and identification via ultracentrifugation, TEM, NTA, and Western blotting of markers (CD63, CD9) with negative control (calnexin). Functional assays include CCK-8, EdU, Transwell (migration/invasion), glycolysis measurements (lactate, glucose, ATP, ECAR). Dual-luciferase reporter confirms miR-448/RAB7A binding. miR-448 mimic transfection generates EXO-miR-448. RT-qPCR validates expression. siRNA knockdown demonstrates RAB7A requirement. However, single primary source for exosomes (HepG2); no patient-derived exosomes; limited to 3 cancer lines.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 5 (preclinical cell-based mechanistic work). Identifies exosomal miR-448 as suppressor of liver cancer proliferation, migration, invasion, and glycolysis via RAB7A targeting. Translational path speculative; no animal models, xenografts, or patient correlation. Proposed therapeutic targeting of miR-448 or RAB7A lacks in vivo validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods detailed with cell culture conditions, exosome isolation protocols, transfection procedures, and assay details. Cell line authentication (STR profiling) and mycoplasma testing mentioned. ARRIVE not applicable (cell-based, not animal). Primer sequences provided in Table I; miRNA sequences listed. However, no data availability statement or code sharing mentioned. Supplementary methodology sparse; replication detail adequate.

novelty_literature.justification: miR-448 as tumor suppressor in liver cancer known (refs 8-11). Exosomal localization of miR-448 and functional role in glycolysis appears novel. RAB7A as miR-448 target newly identified. Combination of exosomal miR-448 + RAB7A + glycolysis is mechanistically novel for this context.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized methods with clear cell culture, exosome isolation, and functional assay descriptions. Results logically presented (expression, exosome characterization, functional validation, target identification, mechanism). Figures appropriate (TEM, NTA, Western, luciferase, functional assays). Discussion contextualizes miRNA and glycolysis in liver cancer. Some sections could be tightened; generally readable and clear.

key_strengths: Rigorous exosome characterization: ultracentrifugation, TEM, NTA, and Western confirmation (CD63, CD9) with negative control (calnexin).
miR-448 encapsulation in exosomes confirmed via RNase A and Triton X-100 treatment.
Multi-method functional validation: CCK-8, EdU, Transwell assays demonstrate EXO-miR-448 inhibits proliferation, migration, invasion.
Mechanistic validation: dual-luciferase reporter confirms miR-448/RAB7A binding; siRNA knockdown rescues phenotype.
Glycolysis inhibition demonstrated: reduced lactate, glucose uptake, ATP, ECAR with EXO-miR-448 treatment.
key_concerns: Limited to single cell line source for exosomes (HepG2); functional validation in exosomes from Hep3B and SK-HEP-1 would strengthen.
No patient-derived exosomes or clinical samples; translational relevance speculative.
No in vivo xenograft or animal model validation; mechanism confirmed only in vitro.
miR-448 target specificity: only RAB7A functionally validated; other predicted targets (SGPP1, VASH2, MPC1, TMSB4X listed in methods) not mechanistically explored.
Glycolysis modulation pathway (how RAB7A affects glucose metabolism) not fully elucidated mechanistically.
No assessment of whether EXO-miR-448 internalization mechanism or miR-448 processing details.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid preclinical mechanistic study identifying exosomal miR-448 as suppressor of liver cancer via RAB7A-mediated glycolysis inhibition. Well-characterized exosomes and comprehensive functional validation. Lacks in vivo confirmation and patient relevance. Suitable for tier 4 specialized journal after minor revisions clarifying target specificity and glycolysis mechanism.
